hero.headline: Jensen Beach's Andrew Burnette wins legal fight for fifth year, returns to Louisiana Tech
hero.body:
Jensen Beach native Andrew Burnette has won back a fifth season of college football eligibility after taking his case to court against the NCAA, and he is now back on the field at Louisiana Tech. Burnette moved to Martin County from Michigan around age 12 and went on to star at Jensen Beach High School, where he originally enrolled to wrestle before football took over as his main focus. "I wasn't zoned for that school, but I went there for wrestling originally; that was my first passion," Burnette said. "Moving through high school, I knew football was what I wanted to do."

Despite his success at Jensen Beach High School, Burnette said he did not draw much interest from college recruiters, a common experience for Treasure Coast football players. "One of my main struggles was recruitment out of high school, because I felt like our area was a little under-recruited," he said. He chose to play at Highland Community College in Kansas, where he rushed for 340 yards and two touchdowns in nine games, but still failed to attract bigger programs. He then transferred to Independence Junior College, a school featured on the Netflix series Last Chance U, but was cut from that team.

Burnette reached out to Keiser University in West Palm Beach, reminding the coaching staff that they had offered him a spot back in high school. "I spoke with the coach there and told him, 'You guys offered me in high school,' and he said, 'I don't really remember. Send me your film.' He saw my film and said, 'Hey, bring it,'" Burnette said. Over two seasons at Keiser, he rushed for more than 2,300 yards and scored 30 touchdowns, numbers that finally caught the attention of Division I programs, including Louisiana Tech. He played his first Division I season there last year, but his NCAA eligibility ran out under the old four-year limit.

Rather than walk away from the game, Burnette called his father and took a job working alongside him at a steel mill in Detroit. "I called my dad and told him, 'Hey, I need to do something. I can't just sit here,' so I went and worked with my dad in Michigan," he said. This summer the NCAA adopted a new 5-in-5 rule, allowing athletes to compete in up to five seasons within a continuous five-year window. Burnette hired a lawyer and took his case to court against the NCAA, which granted him a final season of eligibility. He is now back on the field at Louisiana Tech. "It was amazing; I would rather play football than do anything, and for me to have this opportunity again, it's a blessing," Burnette said.

hero.headline: Injury Crash Backs Up Florida's Turnpike for 2 Miles Near Stuart
hero.body:
A crash with injuries on northbound Florida's Turnpike near Stuart is causing a two-mile traffic backup in Martin County. The crash was reported near mile marker 129 shortly after 2:15 p.m. Sunday, according to FL511.

FL511 reported the right lane blocked between mile markers 127 and 129 as of 2:46 p.m. Florida Highway Patrol information listed no roadblock in the area.

Drivers should use caution and expect delays on the northbound Turnpike while crews respond. This is a developing story.

According to FL511, the crash was reported shortly after 2:15 p.m. and was causing a backup of about 2 miles on the northbound Turnpike. FL511 also reported the right lane blocked between mile markers 127 and 129 as of 2:46 p.m. Florida Highway Patrol information listed no roadblock. hero.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty, Brother Died in 2025
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died on duty Saturday, just over a year after his brother Jarius died while serving in the same role. The Hodge family had publicly pushed for accountability after Jarius's 2025 death at a Port St. Lucie hospital.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, Oct. 24, more than a year after his younger brother Jarius Hodge, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died at age 26. The district announced Austin's line-of-duty death Saturday, calling it a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Austin Hodge had joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years, most recently assigned to Station 9. Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue also shared condolences following his unexpected death Saturday morning. The circumstances surrounding Austin's death have not been released, and the fire district asked the public to respect his family's privacy as they grieve.

Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025, after becoming ill with the flu he contracted from a patient at work earlier that month. Austin said his brother had been healthy before getting sick and alleged that medical staff made critical errors in his treatment, including taking three attempts to intubate him.

The brothers shared a close bond built around their shared career in firefighting. "This was my best friend, my twin," Austin said of Jarius in the earlier interview. "We had the same hairstyle." He described his brother as someone who loved going to work and loved working alongside him. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

After Jarius's death, Austin spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," Austin said. He stressed that the family wanted accountability, not money. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable." The St. Lucie County Fire District said it will share information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor Austin Hodge's service once details are finalized in coordination with his family.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Newspaper Delivery Driver in NW California Boulevard Hit-and-Run
cards.teaser: A geofence warrant and matching vehicle fasteners helped detectives crack the two-week case, but police say they are still looking for a second vehicle.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a 60-year-old newspaper delivery driver in connection with the Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old resident critically injured on NW California Boulevard. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.

The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains in critical condition at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. Niemczyk said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash happened.

Investigators spent two weeks reviewing video, physical evidence and other leads before making an arrest. Niemczyk said a geofence warrant seeking cellphone location data from the crash area and time produced a lead showing Aude's phone had pinged off cell towers there at the time of the crash, pointing detectives toward Aude and vehicles registered to him. Detectives then located and examined his vehicle, which had damage to the front bumper and hood consistent with striking a pedestrian, along with presumptive positive results for blood that require further testing. cards.article_text: A 60-year-old man was arrested in connection with a hit-and-run crash that critically injured a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie resident, police said. The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. 9 on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains in critical condition at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Ft. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. He said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash happened. Investigators reviewed video, physical evidence and other leads since the crash two weeks ago. Niemczyk said a geofence warrant which sought cellphone location data from a specific area during a specific time produced a lead showing Aude's phone had pinged off cell phone towers in that area at the time of the crash. That helped detectives identify Aude as the alleged hit and run driver and the vehicles registered to him. Detectives then located and examined the man’s vehicle, which had damage consistent with striking a pedestrian, including damage to the front bumper and hood, Niemczyk said. Investigators also found presumptive positive results for blood on the vehicle. Further testing is needed. Police also recovered pieces of the vehicle’s inner fender-well fasteners at the scene, Niemczyk said. Detectives found that several matching fasteners were missing from the suspect’s vehicle. Investigators are still looking for a second vehicle that was traveling southbound near the crash. Niemczyk said distant video showed a vehicle traveling in each direction, but it was difficult to determine what happened. Police are trying to learn whether the second vehicle also struck the victim or if the driver of the second vehicle witnessed the accident. We’re very confident that the vehicle that we have and the person that we’ve arrested are responsible for the majority of what occurred, Niemczyk said. The Police Chief said the victim was in the middle of the road when he was struck, but investigators could not determine from the video whether he was walking or jogging. Police learned he often exercised at night when the weather was cooler and he was known to walk on the road and medians. "I've been doing this for 30 years. I'm not surprised by a whole lot anymore. I've seen pedestrians left for dead on the side of the road before. It doesn't make it any easier, but it doesn't surprise me at this point either. It's just difficult to understand how one human being could be so, you know, without compassion for another," Chief Niemczyk said. See also: 2 arrested in killing of transgender woman Jayla McGee in Belle Glade The victim had no identification or cellphone with him, Niemczyk said. cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Newspaper Driver in Hit-and-Run That Critically Injured Pedestrian
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a newspaper delivery driver in connection with a hit-and-run crash two weeks ago that left a 63-year-old man critically injured. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested 60-year-old Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.

The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains in critical condition at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. Niemczyk said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash happened.

Detectives spent two weeks reviewing video, physical evidence and other leads before identifying Aude as a suspect. Niemczyk said a geofence warrant seeking cellphone location data from the crash area during the time of the crash showed Aude's phone had pinged off cell towers there, helping investigators trace the vehicles registered to him. hero.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty, One Year After Brother's Death
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter/paramedic Austin Hodge, 34, died Saturday morning while on duty, the agency said. His death comes one year after his brother, Jarius Hodge, also a firefighter with the district, died after falling ill at work.

Austin Hodge joined the St. Lucie County Fire District on July 17, 2017, and was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce. On Saturday morning, a procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies escorted him from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce. The St. Lucie County Fire District called his death "a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," and extended "heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time."

Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at Station 3, where he worked. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. On May 30, people gathered to celebrate what would have been his 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. At that gathering, Austin Hodge said of his brother, "He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today." In May, another district firefighter, 21-year-old Connor Whitehead, also died, though the cause of his death was not released.

In the hours after Austin Hodge's death, firefighters, the district's Honor Guard and public safety partners gathered to honor him, the fire district said on Facebook. "The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station," the district wrote. "It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another." The district credited the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties with offering "strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves." Condolences also came in from Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, the Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. The St. Lucie County Fire District operates 20 fire stations with 523 firefighters countywide. Information on memorial arrangements and ways to honor Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies, One Year After Brother's Death
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge, 34, died Saturday morning while on duty, the agency confirmed. Hodge was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce and had served with the district since July 17, 2017. His death comes just over a year after his brother, Jarius Hodge, also a firefighter-paramedic with the district, died after falling ill at Station 3.

A procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies escorted Austin Hodge from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce on Saturday morning. Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025, after his family said he came down with the flu, felt weak at work and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. Family and friends gathered on May 30 to mark what would have been Jarius Hodge's 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today."

Austin Hodge's death marks the third loss of a St. Lucie County firefighter in recent months. Firefighter Connor Whitehead, 21, died on May 31, though the cause of his death was not released. The St. Lucie County Fire District operates 20 fire stations and employs 523 firefighters across the county, according to the agency.

The St. Lucie County Fire District called Hodge's death "a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," extending "heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." In a Facebook post, the agency said, "In the hours following this heartbreaking loss, our firefighters, Honor Guard, and public safety partners came together to honor our fallen brother and stand alongside one another during an incredibly difficult time. The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station. It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another. Today, that bond was especially evident through the incredible support of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. Together, they offered strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves. Our hearts are with Austin's family, loved ones, and everyone who had the privilege of serving alongside him. We are deeply grateful to our fellow first responders and community for the outpouring of support during this tremendous loss." Condolences also came from Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, the Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. The St. Lucie County Fire District said information on memorial arrangements and ways to honor Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Police: Missing 5-Year-Old Found Dead in Pond Near Portofino Landing
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police say a 5-year-old nonverbal girl who went missing from her apartment complex Saturday was found dead hours later in a nearby pond, with investigators now revealing new details about the search effort, including an attempt to track her location through a tablet she had with her. Mayra Glory Odelus was last seen before noon in the 5100 block of Portofino Landing Apartments east of Interstate 95. Her body was discovered in the pond at about 3 p.m., roughly 75 yards from her apartment, about three hours after she was reported missing. Police received the initial report at 11:39 a.m., and family members told officers Mayra was autistic and nonverbal.

She was last seen wearing a dark oversized shirt with two white beads in her hair. Officers searched the surrounding area, handed out flyers with her name and photo, and flew drones over the area. Police called in Port St. Lucie bloodhounds and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office dive team, which conducted an underwater search that led to the discovery of her body. According to police spokesperson Michael Santiago, Mayra had a tablet with her when she disappeared, and her family tried to locate her by pinging the device. The ping led searchers to the pond area, but at that point there was no sign of her, and the tablet itself has still not been recovered.

Mayra's father told police the pond sits directly across from their apartment and that she loved the water. He and Mayra's 18-year-old sister were home at the time she went missing. Her mother lives in Haiti and was expected to arrive Sunday. "Our deepest condolences are with Mayra's family and loved ones during this tragic time," the Fort Pierce Police Department said in a statement. Santiago added, "It's very tragic when anything like this happens, but with our kids we have to make sure we're paying attention all the time, especially when kids are challenged with autism."

Drowning remains the leading cause of unintentional death among children ages 1 to 3. Dr. Elizabeth Feldman of Cleveland Clinic Florida has said drowning can happen within seconds, and a lack of oxygen for just a few minutes can cause brain injury. The Children's Services Council of Palm Beach reported that 39 children with autism or suspected autism drowned in Florida in 2025, the highest number ever recorded in the state. The case has renewed attention on tracking and safety devices designed to prevent or respond to water-related emergencies involving children with autism, many of whom are drawn to water and may wander from supervision without being able to call for help.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty, Year After Brother's Death
cards.teaser: Austin Hodge, a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic who publicly pushed for medical malpractice accountability after his brother's 2025 death, died while on duty Saturday.
cards.body:
A St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic died while on duty Saturday morning, more than a year after his younger brother, who also served as a firefighter-paramedic for the district, died at age 26. The St. Lucie County Fire District announced the line-of-duty death of Austin Hodge on Saturday, Oct. 24, calling it a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9. Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue also shared condolences following his unexpected death. The circumstances surrounding Austin Hodge's death have not been released. The fire district asked the public to respect his family's privacy as they grieve and said information about memorial arrangements will be shared once finalized.

Austin Hodge's death comes more than a year after his younger brother, Jarius Hodge, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died on July 22, 2025. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. "We had the same hairstyle." He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

In that earlier interview, Austin said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025. He said his brother went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22, struggling to breathe, but died hours later. Austin alleged that medical staff made critical errors in treating Jarius, including taking three attempts to intubate him, and said his brother had been healthy before becoming ill.

Austin also spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for his brother's death. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," he said. He emphasized that his family was seeking accountability rather than financial compensation. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable." The St. Lucie County Fire District said additional information about ways to honor Austin Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family.

The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. This was my best friend, my twin, Austin Hodge previously told CBS12 News. We had the same hairstyle. He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him, Austin said. He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country. Family sought accountability after Jarius’ death In an interview with CBS12 News , Austin said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025. Austin said his younger brother went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22, struggling to breathe, but died hours later. He alleged that medical staff made critical errors in treating his brother, including taking three attempts to intubate him. He said Jarius had been healthy before becoming ill. Austin also spoke publicly about Florida’s medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for Jarius’ death. This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long, Austin said in the earlier interview. He emphasized that his family was seeking accountability rather than financial compensation. For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar, he said. We just want those physicians to be held accountable. The circumstances surrounding Austin Hodge’s death have not been released. Lucie County Fire District said additional information about ways to honor his service will be shared in coordination with his family.
